annotations.text:
KaizenOS mobile app — 390 × 844

Restructured as a native app, not a port of the web build. The web version is one canvas with everything stacked on it as modals; that does not survive contact with a phone.

FOUR TABS. Kaiso (the session), Plan, Library, You. Progress and outputs are destinations, not overlays — you can check either without covering the conversation, and get anywhere without going home first.

THE SESSION GOES IMMERSIVE. B1 is home, with the tab bar. The moment a session is live (B2, B3) the tab bar and chrome recede: one line of context up top, one control row at the bottom — mute, end, scribe. Nothing competes with the voice.

TIME, NOT TOKENS. Everywhere a founder sees their balance it reads "14 min left". Tokens are the billing unit; minutes are what they are actually spending, and what they can act on.

Safe areas reserved, not drawn: 59pt top, 34pt bottom.

Session states

B4 the scribe is a real sheet with a grabber, not a fixed 70% panel — it drags between peek and full.

B5 replaces the old toast-plus-badge. A ready asset arrives as a banner with a View action, on screen long enough to act on. No badge to hunt down afterwards, which was the whole of KAIZ-117.

B7 sells more time at the moment it runs out, and says plainly that nothing was lost. B8 and B9 make the same promise — that is the anxiety in a voice product.

Plan

Three levels: all nine pillars (C1), the nodes inside one (C2), then a single node (C3).

C3 is the screen the web build has no equivalent for, and it is what makes the plan more than a progress bar: what Kaiso already has, what is still missing, the question it will ask next, and a button to go talk about exactly that. It turns a status list into a way in.

Pillar colours are the wheel’s own. Node names are the live build’s, including the deferred Virtue pillar.

First run

Intake is now a stepped native form — a nav bar with Step n of 4 and a Skip, one thin progress rule, a large title, and 44pt+ controls throughout. It was a scrolling card floating in space, which is a web layout.

A10 is the profile Kaiso builds from the intake; A11 and A12 keep the emailed copy, since that is still how the report is delivered.

Dropped in this round: the standalone onboarding tour and the mic priming screen. Both were teaching a UI that no longer needs teaching — four labelled tabs and one Start talking button. Permission is asked at the first tap of Start talking, in context, where the OS prompt belongs.

Library

A tab, not a modal. Assets are cards with real state; tapping opens a full-screen document with a nav bar and the system share sheet — not a card inside a card.

D2 is the first-run state: an empty library is the most common thing a new user sees, so it explains what will appear and offers the one action that makes it happen.

[YOUR RAISE AMOUNT] on D3 is a deliberate placeholder — do not ship it as written.

D7–D9 are the three outputs added after the first round. The pitch is a segmented control rather than three stacked blocks — ninety seconds of spoken copy is a wall of text at 390pt. The org chart drops the branching tree for a grouped list, because a tree does not survive this width; state moves into a pill. The brand kit keeps the mark picker, since choosing a direction is the one thing a founder will actually do on a phone.

You

Replaces the corner dropdown, which was a web pattern that hid five destinations behind one avatar.

Time remaining is the first thing on the screen with an Add time action beside it, because running out mid-conversation is the failure this product has.

E3 sells hours, not tokens. E4 is the platform subscription sheet — StoreKit / Play Billing, not the web card form.

E2 is redrawn out of the default Clerk chrome.
